manager_rule: When failing_reasons for round R contains exactly one net of a Kelvin pair for cable N — specifically /SENSEC{N}_HI appears with 'has unconnected ratlines' but /SENSEC{N}_LO does NOT (or vice versa) — the manager MUST log 'partial_kelvin_pair_failure' with fields: (a) round number, (b) cable index N, (c) the failing net name, (d) the routed partner net name, (e) unconnected ratline count for the failing net, (f) absorbed and trimmed_spurs counts from the stub summary. On the immediately following round the stub compiler MUST emit at least one stub targeting exclusively the failing net's source-pad-to-INA-input connection — NOT a symmetric pair stub covering both HI and LO — and that stub MUST be forwarded to FR bypassing the absorber's merge logic, because the routed partner net's existing copper may cause the absorber to classify the asymmetric stub as topologically redundant and silently discard it before FR sees it. This non-absorbable asymmetric stub is additive to any symmetric pair stubs that Rules 19 and 21 would generate for cable N; it does not replace those stubs. If the partial failure for cable N persists for 3 consecutive rounds with the asymmetric non-absorbable stub active, the manager MUST escalate immediately for physical routing geometry inspection of the failing net's pad connections and any keepout regions adjacent to its pads, without waiting for Rule-26's kelvin_fail_streak ceiling.
